decisions.quote: 097821, OR = 1.10 (CI = 0.89-1.37); rs2477686, OR = 1.11 (CI = 0.87-1.43); rs10842262, OR = 1.11 (CI = 0.94-1.32); and rs6080550, OR = 0.96 (CI = 0.76-1.21). None of the SNPs was significantly associated with NOA (P > 0.05). However, three of four SNPs (rs12097821, rs2477686, and rs10842262) showed associations in the same direction in Japanese men as those reported in the Chinese GWAS. To determine whether the four SNPs are genetic risk factors for NOA, the effect sizes of NOA risk factors require further investigation using larger independent sets of case-control samples of populations, including Japanese and Chinese populations.
decisions.reason: Primary Table 1 and Figure 2 of Hu et al. (2011, 10.1038/ng.1040; hu_table.txt, hu_figure.txt) confirm that the bound original Chinese GWAS (N=2,927 cases, 5,734 controls) reported combined genome-wide significant NOA associations (P<5e-8) across all four exact SNPs: rs12097821 (OR=1.25), rs2477686 (OR=1.39), rs10842262 (OR=1.23)—all three replicated in Validation I and II—and rs6080550 (combined OR=1.27, P=2.17e-9, though non-significant in Validation II, OR=1.13, P=0.10). Sato et al. (2013, 2b4faa1d0d497c42.txt; complete abstract, with pages 2-4 unavailable) tested all four SNPs across two Japanese cohorts (490 NOA patients, 1,167 controls) combined by meta-analysis specifically 'to evaluate whether SNP loci are associated with NOA' and 'To assess the significance of the associations'. In the meta-analysis, 'None of the SNPs was significantly associated with NOA (P > 0.05)' (rs12097821 OR=1.10, CI=0.89-1.37; rs2477686 OR=1.11, CI=0.87-1.43; rs10842262 OR=1.11, CI=0.94-1.32; rs6080550 OR=0.96, CI=0.76-1.21). Under the codebook, non-significant same-direction point estimates on three SNPs do not constitute partial replication ('mixed'), and requesting larger future studies to determine whether the SNPs are risk factors does not make a completed meta-analysis 'uninformative' or 'cannot_determine'.

prior_decisions.quote: Recently, a Chinese genomewide association study (GWAS) identified four autosomal single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) loci as being significantly associated with risk factors for nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA; P < 5 × 10(-8)). In the present study, we performed a replication study on two Japanese cohorts from different institutions in order to evaluate whether SNP loci are associated with NOA. The four SNPs (rs12097821, rs2477686, rs10842262, and rs6080550) reported in the Chinese GWAS were genotyped in 490 NOA patients and 1167 controls.
prior_decisions.reason: The supplied primary source text (2b4faa1d0d497c42.txt) contains only the title, author list, and abstract, without any in-text citation or reference list. The abstract states that the authors performed a replication study in two Japanese cohorts genotyping 'four SNPs (rs12097821, rs2477686, rs10842262, and rs6080550) reported in the Chinese GWAS' that 'identified four autosomal single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) loci as being significantly associated with risk factors for nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA; P < 5 × 10(-8))'. Although shipped_rows row 2410 is a Chinese NOA GWAS by Hu et al. (2011, Nature Genetics, DOI 10.1038/ng.1040, 'A genome-wide association study in Chinese men identifies three risk loci for non-obstructive azoospermia'), bibliography_metadata.json for 10.1038/ng.1040 contains no abstract or SNP identifiers, and the abstract-only primary text does not provide the authors, year, title, or DOI of the Chinese GWAS or establish whether the four SNPs/loci come exclusively from shipped row 2410 or involve another report. The unresolved question is whether the unnamed Chinese GWAS in the abstract is identical to shipped row 2410 (Hu et al., 2011) with no additional unshipped target. Prior adjudication and state files do not exist for this work.
